findings.reason: without a depends-on entry or a followup naming them, two ready-to-build sections are invisible to the queue and s49/s50 land only if someone remembers them.
findings.text: s49 and s50 were added `implementable` in `plan-section-declarations` (line 23) but `plan-section-depends-on` (line 22) still ends at `s45`, and the only open followup (`f-wns-002`, lines 331-335) names §48 then §45, so a coordinator following the plan's own chain never dispatches either new section

findings.reason: the same file-overlap defect was raised for §45/§48 and fixed by adding a wait; leaving this pair unsequenced repeats the collision the plan has already paid for.
findings.text: s50's repair writes `reckon/crew/runs.py` and `reckon/crew/resumption.py`, both of which are in s48's declared write paths, and both sections are `implementable` with no `depends-on` and no sequencing note, so a wave could dispatch them concurrently into the same two files

findings.reason: a node whose declared write scope omits the test file cannot satisfy its done-when, so this stops the work rather than merely slowing it.
findings.text: s49's and s50's done-whens each require a new `tests/test_*.py`, yet neither section ends with a `Write paths:` sentence, and `code_review_paths_from_plan` reads exactly that sentence (`_WRITE_PATHS_SENTENCE`, `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:4914-4940`) to decide which modules an implementable section claims, so both sections contribute no path at all and a node fenced from its brief cannot create the test its own gate demands

findings.reason: the section is the only place the plan states this obligation for a node, and a missing log path is the failure the manifest's `test_logs` cannot repair after the fact.
findings.text: unlike §46, §47 and §48, s49's and s50's done-whens say nothing about where gate logs go or that they start with the revision and command and end in `EXIT=`, so nothing in the section keeps the evidence off a scratch path or makes the receipt re-runnable

findings.reason: the plan would send a node at the shared helper with no guard that the other writers keep the carry-forward, and the test cannot catch the regression it introduces.
findings.text: s50 says "a resume or redispatch writes the launching host of its new attempt onto the pointer in place of the earlier attempt's" but names no write site, and the symbol it cites as the defect, `runs._stamp_pointer_launch_host` (`reckon/crew/runs.py:403-433`), carries a foreign host forward deliberately: any write of an existing pointer from another machine (the station sweeps at `resumption.py:227, 239, 1593, 1899, 1944`, and coordinators) must not invent its own host, and the stated done-when exercises neither, so changing the helper to stamp `socket.gethostname()` unconditionally passes the plan's test while re-stamping every run the station touches
